evidence: Enumerated every criterion (27): functional 16, polish 5, visual 4, render 1, constraints 1. Functional (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml): every criterion names concrete browser actions through rendered controls (post, reply, edit, delete, hold, timer, wall, copy-link, mark-unread, search, transcript, restart_app) and concrete observable outcomes with quoted text: e.g. signin_and_client_scope 'matter list shows "Pryce lease dispute" and "Pryce will" and not "Marsh Holdings acquisition"'; nested_replies 'JUDGE-R1B sits under JUDGE-R0 after JUDGE-R1's branch, not after JUDGE-RX'; timer_changes 'the probate message disappears at once ... thread shows 7 days beside the title'; persistence re-reads after a real restart_app call. Durable evidence: the prompt requires every refusal to pair with a re-read ('A refusal writes nothing and a re-read matches the previous state'), a same-kind positive control ('Every refusal pairs with a success of the same kind on an eligible target'), hidden/disabled controls do not count as enforcement, and quoting of observed titles/text/marks. No criterion grades a source read, a 'looks right' impression, or a response shape without a state check: replay refusals are each followed by a readback in another account (e.g. CS1 'check as harriet@kittle.test that M-12 has no JUDGE-CS1', WL1 'as Harriet M-13 has no JUDGE-WL1', E1 'still reads "Version two JUDGE-E1"', H0 'is still not on hold', timer '1 day ... after a reload M-13 still shows 30 days'). Distinctive probes: every created value carries a unique JUDGE-* token (CS1, W0, L1, M1, M2, WL0/WL1, R0-R3/R1B/RX, X0/X1, H0-H3/H1C, E1, F1/F2, P1-P3, U1-U3, D1/D2, O, LB/LG/LA/LR/LE/LV, T0/T1, S0-S2, G1); grep -c JUDGE returns 0 in environment/assets/seed_data.json, server.js, app.js and index.html, so none is pre-satisfied. Seeded negatives use specific seed text ('original lease scan', 'Boundary note: rent review date is 5 June.', 'Insurer letter', 'heads of terms', 'Fenwick', 'notice recieved'). Timing claims are decidable without sub-second probes: the fixed clock (integration.md:40) makes the exactly-seven-day/one-second-younger seed boundary deterministic, and live checks use 'within about ten seconds' against the public five-second promise (conversations.md:31). Executability: the scripted golden Playwright run (golden-run.log, hashes verified, source hashes match frozen bytes) carried out the browser steps of all 16 functional criteria in order plus gate_constraints and polish_refusal_in_place and recorded PASS for each, with a real process restart; this shows the steps are performable in a browser and decidable against a conforming app (it is not a configured judge run, Oracle or model score). Polish criteria are concrete visible checks (timer beside title without opening a menu; On hold mark visible without hover; documentElement.scrollWidth equals viewport at 390x844 and the box reachable; replies visibly indented in transcript; refusal reason in words next to the form after ~10 s). Visual criteria are craft likert with described 0-5 anchors and named surfaces/viewports, the accepted shipped format per SKILL.md known false positives; they are inherently aesthetic, not a decidability defect. Gates are concrete (constraints gate posts JUDGE-G1, reloads, and reads it back from a separate context). Weak app considered: a client-only UI hiding M-12 controls or a static facade would fail because replays plus cross-account readbacks are required; a server that accepts writes but forgets them fails persistence restart readback. Conforming alternatives considered: different routes, payload shapes, cookie names and time formats are explicitly accepted ('Any endpoint path, payload shape or cookie name is acceptable'; 'any clear format'). Notes (not defects for this row): (1) timer_changes step 2 asks that replaying the earlier-versions request for a timer-deleted message 'returns not-available'; the public text only promises 'everything about it goes' and reserves 'plain not available' wording for walls/other clients, so an app returning 200 with an empty list could be read strictly; the golden returns 404 'Not available.' (server.js:361-368 via message lookup), and a wall-enforcing app must look the message up first, so a conforming-alternative failure is unlikely. (2) sent_once_in_order Part B requires each message to show '2026-05-12 11:00 (any clear format) in the thread'; the public text says new messages 'carry that time' (integration.md:40) but does not explicitly require a per-message time in the thread; a thread showing only '11:00' may be judged inconsistently. This is a coverage/hidden-requirement question for the rows that own it, flagged for the owner, not a decidability failure. Full configured LLM judge decidability and per-criterion workload remain unmeasured (raw-evidence-index scope says so); those are owned by other rows and are not claimed here.
